# Creating packages with ezpm

This page is for developers and hosts who prefer a script to the browser. `ezpm.php` in the installation root (also
`php bin/php/console ezpm`) is the command line package manager; it makes the same class, content and extension
packages as the [package wizard](creating-packages-with-the-wizard.md), and because it is a command, the export of
your demo content can be repeated for every release with the same options.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit the finished site package by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth: see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## The commands you need

From `php ezpm.php help` and `kernel/private/classes/commands/ezpm.php`:

| Command | Usage | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `create` | `create NAME [SUMMARY [VERSION [INSTALLTYPE]]]` | a new, empty package; `INSTALLTYPE` is `install` (default) or `import` |
| `add` | `add PACKAGE ITEM [ITEMPARAMETERS]...` | adds `ezcontentclass`, `ezcontentobject` (alias `ezcontentsubtree`), `group`, and items of other handlers such as `ezextension` |
| `set` | `set PACKAGE ATTRIBUTE ATTRIBUTEVALUE` | `summary`, `description`, `vendor`, `priority`, `type`, `extension`, `source`, `version`, `licence`, `state` |
| `export` | `export PACKAGE [-d DIRECTORY] [--format=xml\|json]` | writes the `.ezpkg` archive |
| `validate` | `validate SOURCE` | checks an archive, a directory or a package name without importing |
| `check` | `check PACKAGE [--all]` | what installing would meet here, by remote ID; writes nothing |
| `list`, `info` | `list`, `info PACKAGE` | the packages of the repositories, one package's details |

Global options include `-s`/`--siteaccess`, `-l`/`--login` with `-p`/`--password` and `-r`/`--repos`; the full table
is on [ezpm: the package manager on the command line](../../../features/6.0/ezpm-package-manager-cli.md).

> **Warning**
> Run ezpm on a test installation. `install` and `import` change the installation; `create`, `add`, `set` and
> `export` only write packages, but `add` of content reads the whole subtree and can take a while.

## A classes package

```bash
php ezpm.php create acme_classes 'Acme content classes' 1.0.0 install
php ezpm.php add acme_classes ezcontentclass article,folder,acme_product
php ezpm.php set acme_classes vendor acme
php ezpm.php set acme_classes type contentclass
php ezpm.php export acme_classes -d var/tmp
```

`add ezcontentclass` takes one argument: class IDs or identifiers, separated by commas. An unknown one stops the
command with "Content class with identifier ... does not exist".

## A content package

```bash
php ezpm.php create acme_site_democontent 'Acme demo content' 1.0.0 install
php ezpm.php add acme_site_democontent ezcontentsubtree /content/demo \
    --exclude-classes --exclude-templates --language=eng-US,ger-DE
php ezpm.php set acme_site_democontent vendor acme
php ezpm.php set acme_site_democontent type contentobject
php ezpm.php export acme_site_democontent -d var/tmp
```

The starting point is a node ID or a URL path; everything below it is included. The options of `add ezcontentobject`:
`--include-classes`/`--exclude-classes`, `--include-templates`/`--exclude-templates`, `--node-main`/`--node-selected`,
`--siteaccess=sa,sa2`, `--language=loc1,loc2`, `--current-version`/`--all-versions`, `--minimal-template-set`. Leave
the classes out when your classes package carries them, so they are defined in one place.

## An extension package

`bin/repack_extension.sh` in the 7x source repository shows the sequence the 7x team used for an extension package:

```bash
php ezpm.php create acme_extension 'Acme extension' '1.0.0' 'install'
php ezpm.php add acme_extension ezextension acme
php ezpm.php set acme_extension vendor acme
php ezpm.php set acme_extension type extension
php ezpm.php set acme_extension state stable
```

Exporting an extension is off by default: `add ezextension` refuses until the extension is listed in
`package.ini [ExtensionExportSettings] AllowedExtensions[]` (or `*`), and it always refuses an extension that holds
secret values or key material ([Exporting with ezpm](../../designers/extensions/exporting-with-ezpm.md)).

## Setting fields

`set` changes one field of the package definition and, like `add` and `delete`, "will open up a new release if no open
releases exists yet" (the command's help). `create` starts every package with release `1`, the license `GPL`, the
state `alpha`, no vendor and the logged-in user (if any) as maintainer. Set at least:

| Attribute | Example | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` | `acme` | the repository directory the package is imported into |
| `type` | `contentclass`, `contentobject`, `extension` | the type the index and the policies use |
| `licence` | `GPL-2.0-or-later` | the license the package page shows ([License and documents](../requirements/license-and-documents.md)) |
| `state` | `stable` | one of `package.ini [PackageSettings] StateList[]` |

## Export, validate, check

```bash
php ezpm.php export acme_classes -d var/tmp                 # classic format
php ezpm.php export acme_classes -d var/tmp --format=json   # JSON format, .json.ezpkg
php ezpm.php validate var/tmp/acme_classes-1.0.0-1.ezpkg
php ezpm.php check acme_site_democontent --all
```

`export` names the archive `<name>-<version>-<release>.ezpkg` (`eZPackage::exportName()`). A package server and an
`index.xml` usually use `<name>.ezpkg`, the name `build.sh` gives: unpack the export into `packages/<name>/` of your
source repository and let `build.sh` make the published archive, so every package of a release is built the same way
([Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md)). The two formats are explained on
[Classic and JSON packages](../basics/classic-and-json-packages.md).

## A release script

Keep the commands in your source repository so the next release repeats them exactly:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd /path/to/test-installation
php ezpm.php create acme_site_democontent 'Acme demo content' "$1" install
php ezpm.php add acme_site_democontent ezcontentsubtree /content/demo --exclude-classes
php ezpm.php set acme_site_democontent vendor acme
php ezpm.php export acme_site_democontent -d "$HOME/acme-build"
```

Run it for a package name that is not in the test installation's repositories yet (`php ezpm.php list` shows them),
so each run starts from an empty package.
